env._reward_mode_notes: 'value' = upstream StockPortfolioEnv (reward = portfolio value, non-stationary, dominates late-period training samples). 'log_return' = LogReturnPortfolioEnv (reward = log(1 + portfolio_return) * reward_scaling). reward_scaling=1.0 is the recommended default for log_return mode; 1e-4 would shrink the signal to ~1e-6 and starve the gradient.
env._transaction_cost_penalty_notes: Per-unit-turnover cost rate used to shape the reward when reward_mode='log_return'. Math: turnover = |w_t - w_{t-1}|.sum(); tc_fraction = transaction_cost_penalty * turnover; net_return = (1 + gross)*(1 - tc_fraction) - 1; reward = log(1 + net_return) * reward_scaling. Set to 0.0 to disable the penalty entirely - the env then behaves identically to ../1.reward_returns/. The default 0.001 matches the broker-level commission used in backtrader_config.json (stage 4 still applies its own broker costs independently; the two cost models do not double-count because they live in different layers).

walk_forward._notes: When enabled=true: stage 2 trains a fresh model per window (saved as models/agent_<algo>_w<i>.zip + a windows.json manifest), and stage 3 stitches per-window predictions into a single continuous out-of-sample equity curve. If 'windows' is a non-null list of [train_start, train_end, eval_start, eval_end] 4-tuples (ISO date strings), it overrides 'auto'. Otherwise windows are auto-generated by sliding a (train_years, eval_years) window forward by step_years from data.train_start_date until eval_start hits data.trade_end_date. Setting enabled=false reproduces the single-split behaviour of ../2.transaction_cost/. Stage 4 (backtrader) does NOT currently swap models per window; it loads only the last window's agent and replays the full out-of-sample period - see README appendix A.13.
